 Order

This revision petition is filed by the accused/revision petitioner challenging the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the VI Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Bengaluru City in C.C.No.14795/2002 dated 17.01.2014 and confirmed by the LI Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City in Crl.A.No.82/2014 dated 10.12.2015.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, parties herein are referred with the original ranks occupied by them before the trial Court.

3. The brief factual matrix leading to the case are that the Police Inspector of S.J.Park Police Station,
submitted the charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 465, 468,
471, 420 and 506 of IPC.

It is the specific contention of the prosecution that, in the year 1993 accused had created forged Army ID card and other documents with an intention to marry the daughter of CW.8 by name NC: 2023:KHC:33794 Priyalatha.
Accordingly, on 31.12.1993 the marriage of the accused was solemnized with CW.9 and out of the said wedlock a child was born.

Thereafter, the accused had left the 1st wife by name Priyalatha and the accused used the forged documents asserting that he is unmarried and highly qualified having obtained degree of M.Tech and LL.B and claiming himself to be an Army officer, on 15.10.1998, he contracted 2nd marriage with CW.11 Arathi.

Subsequently, it was brought to the knowledge of CW.11 and her brother who is the complainant, that the accused is not an Army officer, and he has created the documents as if he is working as a commander in Army, in order to cheat CW.9 and CW.11.

It is the further assertion that, the accused had threatened the complainant and when the same was questioned he quarreled with the complainant and he also had taken 2,00,000/- from CW.8 and later on married daughter of CW.6 and therefore it is alleged that the accused has committed the offences as alleged.

4. On the basis of the complaint lodged by the complainant, the investigating officer investigated the NC: 2023:KHC:33794 matter, apprehended the accused and recovered the fake ID card from his custody.
He has also recorded the statement of material witnesses and found that, there are sufficient grounds to proceed against the accused and hence, he submitted the charge sheet against the accused.

sentences.text: After submission of the charge sheet, as there are sufficient grounds to proceed against the accused, learned Magistrate has taken cognizance of the offences.
The accused was initially arrested and remanded to custody, but subsequently, he was enlarged on bail.

He was represented by the counsel and the prosecution papers were furnished to him as contemplated under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
6.
After hearing the learned APP and the learned counsel appearing for the accused, the learned Magistrate has framed charges under Sections 465, 468, 471, 420 and 506 of IPC.
The charges were read over and explained to the accused.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
To prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined 17 witnesses and also got marked 13 documents.

After conclusion of the evidence of the prosecution, the statement of accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. is recorded to enable the accused to explain the incriminating evidence appearing against him in the case of the prosecution.
The case of the accused is of total denial.

8. After having heard the arguments and after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, the learned Magistrate has convicted the accused for all the offences by imposing sentence period of six months with a fine of Rs.2000/- for each offence, and further directed that all the sentence shall run concurrently with default clause.
9. Being aggrieved by this judgment of conviction and order of sentence, the accused has approached the learned LI Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City in Crl.A.No.82/2014.

entities.text: LI Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The learned Sessions Judge after re-appreciating the oral and documentary NC:
2023:KHC:33794 evidence, dismissed the appeal by confirming the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the learned Magistrate.
Being aggrieved by this concurrent findings, the revision petitioner is before this Court.
10. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the revision petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent/State.
Perused the records.
11. Learned counsel for the revision petitioner would contend that, the ingredients of the offences punishable under Sections 465, 468, 479, 420 and 506 of IPC are not attracted.

He would also contend that though all the witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution but they are all interested witnesses and the revision petitioner never claimed himself to be an Army officer and highly qualified such as M.Tech degree holder and LL.B degree holder, but all these allegations were made by the complainant, as the accused married the sister of the complainant against the wish of complainant and under the apprehension that, he would have to forego NC: 2023:KHC:33794 half of the share in the property.
He would also assert that the evidence led by the prosecution is not sufficient and both the Courts below have committed a error in convicting him.
Hence, he would seek for allowing the revision.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader would support the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by both the Courts below.
He would contend that the complainant and all the material witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution.

He would further assert that the 1st wife as well as 2nd wife have corroborated the allegations made against the accused and further the fake ID Card was recovered from the custody of the accused under Ex.P3 and Ex.P5 clearly disclose that the accused disclosed his ID card and his status as Army Captain and further having multiple degrees in M.Tech, LL.B etc.

He would contend that the evidence available would clearly establish that the accused, in order to marry Priyalatha had disclosed his false identity and subsequently, after having deserted her, NC: 2023:KHC:33794 during subsistence of the 1st marriage again contracted 2nd marriage with Arathi on the same set of facts, by claiming himself to be an Army officer.
He would also assert that both the Courts below have appreciated the oral and documentary evidence in proper prospective and have rightly convicted the accused.
Hence, he would contend that, the judgment of conviction and order of sentence does not call for any interference and sought for dismissal of the revision.
13. Having heard the arguments and after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, now the following point would arise for my consideration.

1. Whether the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the learned Magistrate and confirmed by the learned Sessions Judge are perverse, arbitrary and erroneous so as to call for any interference by this Court?
14. The allegations of the prosecution discloses that the accused got himself introduced as an Army officer and married CW.8 Priyalatha on 31.12.1993.

It is alleged that NC: 2023:KHC:33794 subsequently, the accused desserted her and then disclosing his status as M.Tech Degree holder and LL.B degree holder and working in Army again contracted marriage with CW.11 Arathi.
15. The complainant is examined as PW.1 and he reiterated the complaint allegations.

He has also specifically deposed that the accused has shown his Army ID card and other records and later on,
against his will he married his sister and stayed in their house.

In the entire cross-examination,
marriage of the accused with Arathi was not at all denied.

A simple suggestion is made asserting that, as complainant is under apprehension that he has to forego half of the property in favour of his sister, he has falsely implicated him by lodging the false complaint, but he denied the said suggestion.
16. PW.2 is the mother of complainant and mother of Arathi CW.1.
She has also supported the case of the prosecution.
PW.4 is the 2nd wife and she has also supported the case of the prosecution and deposed in terms of the prosecution.
PW.6 A.Mutthu is the father of - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:33794 CW.9 and he has also supported that, the case of the prosecution.

He deposed that he came in contact with the accused in 1993 when they were proceeding to Vellur in train and subsequently, the accused developed intimacy by visiting their house, by disclosing his status as Sri.

sentences.text: Army captain and later on married his daughter.
He has also deposed that he had paid Rs.2,00,000/- to the accused out of his retirement benefit.
Though the witness was cross-examined at length, in the entire evidence there is no denial of the case of the prosecution specifically.

But a inconsistent and contradictory suggestion was made to PW.6 asserting that the marriage of the accused was not solemnized with the complainant, but it is not the case of the prosecution that, the complainant was married with the accused.
On the contrary, it is admitted that the marriage was settled by consent of the parties and invitation card was prepared as per Ex.P5.
A simple suggestion was made that, marriage was not solemnized as per Ex.P5, but he denied the said suggestion and he asserts that only reception was not arranged.
PW.7-Priyalatha is the victim girl being 1st wife of the accused.
She also deposed against the accused regarding he marrying her under the false pretext of working as a captain in Army and highly qualified person.

In the entire cross-examination there is no serious challenge to the marriage and it is simply asserted that though, the marriage card was printed as per Ex.P5 marriage did not take place, but she denied the said suggestion.
There are no reasons for these two witnesses to give false evidence against the accused.
18. PW.8 is a seizure spot mahazar witness and he has deposed having drawn Ex.P2 mahazar where they had seized Ex.P4 under the mahazar Ex.P2.
PW9 has deposed regarding the accused abusing complainant.
PW.11 has also deposed to this effect.
PW.12 has specifically deposed that, the accused was staying on rent in her house and he claimed to be an Army officer and shown Ex.P4.
Even the evidence of PW.13 supports the case of the prosecution.
PW.3 is the brother of PW.7 and he is son is PW.6, who has also supported the case of the prosecution.
. On perusal of the oral and documentary evidence, it is evident that accused discloses is identity as a captain, working in Army intelligence.
Ex. P4
is recovered from the custody of the accused and Ex.P5 the marriage invitation card clearly discloses his status as Army captain.
Though the accused has denied the marriage with PW.7, the evidence of PWs.3, 6 and 7 clearly establish that accused was married to PW.7 by falsely disclosing his status and there by cheated her.
He has also created a false document as Army intelligence officer.
The oral and documentary evidence clearly establish that, accused cheated not only PW.7, but also her family members as well as his 2nd wife PW.4.
Both the Courts have appreciated the oral and documentary evidence and have rightly convicted the accused.
No illegality and infirmity is found in the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the trial Court.
Sri. Sanjay Raman vs State By S.J. Park Police Station

Learned Magistrate has also imposed reasonable sentence for six months with fine of Rs.2,000/-
for each sentences and further directed that, all the - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:33794 sentences shall run concurrently.

Hence, it is evident that the learned Magistrate has also imposed a reasonable sentence of six months which does not call for any interference.
21.

Considering the motive on the part of the accused in committing the offences, no grounds are forthcoming to interfere with the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by both the Courts below.

As such, the point under consideration is answered in the negative and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER 1. The revision petition is dismissed.
2.

The impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by VI Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru City in C.C.No.14795/2002 dated 17.01.2014 and confirmed by the LI Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge,
Bengaluru City in Crl.A.No.82/2014 dated 10.12.2015 stands confirmed.
